attributes.description: Alerts when the count of firewall (WAF) requests with a 'deny' action exceeds 100 in a 10-minute window. An elevated deny rate can indicate an active attack (DDoS, credential stuffing, crawling) or an overly restrictive firewall rule change blocking legitimate traffic.
attributes.name: [Vercel OTel] Firewall deny spike

investigation_guide.blob:
## Firewall Deny Spike

### Triage Steps
1. Sample the denied requests: `FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default | WHERE vercel.log.source == "firewall" | EVAL waf_action = FIELD_EXTRACT(vercel.proxy, "waf_action") | WHERE waf_action == "deny" | KEEP @timestamp, url.path, client.address, user_agent.original | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 100`
2. Check whether denies are concentrated on a small number of client IPs (`client.address`) or user agents — this points to a targeted attack rather than a rule misconfiguration.
3. Check whether denies are spread across many paths/IPs but started right after a firewall rule change — review recent audit log `event_name` values related to firewall/rule configuration.
4. If this is a genuine attack, no action may be required (the WAF is doing its job) — but consider notifying security/on-call if the volume is large enough to risk collateral impact (e.g. rate-limit exhaustion).
5. If legitimate traffic is being blocked, review and relax the offending firewall rule.

### Note
`vercel.log.source == "firewall"` covers all WAF-processed requests, including `log`-only actions that are not actually blocked. This rule filters specifically to `waf_action == "deny"` via `FIELD_EXTRACT` to isolate real blocks.

### Escalation
Escalate to the security team if deny volume exceeds 10x the normal baseline or if source IPs correlate with known threat intelligence.
